documents.author: MA
documents.body: Med rec at rooming. Patient has a new bottle: nifedipine ER 30 mg daily, prescribed by his cardiologist. Pharmacy fill history confirms first fill 01/08/2025. Not on our list; no cardiology letter from that visit on file. Added as outside med. Other meds unchanged. Allergy: iodinated contrast, severe.

documents.title: Office Visit: leg swelling
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: ankles swelling.

HPI: 71 y/o with CAD (prior MI, LAD stent), stable angina, HTN, and the contrast reaction during his aborted cath in September. Cardiology added nifedipine ER 30 mg at his January visit for the angina and pressure; we did not get a note, med rec today from his bottle and the pharmacy. About 3 weeks ago his ankles and feet started swelling. Heavy by evening, shoes tight by supper, almost gone when he gets up. No shortness of breath, no orthopnea, no PND. No chest pain or palpitations lately and the chest pressure is less frequent since nifedipine. No weight gain he's noticed. Hasn't traveled, no diet change, hasn't been laid up.
ROS: no muscle aches, no urinary symptoms, no rash or skin changes, appetite fine, not tired, not dizzy. Sleeping well. Still walks the dog every morning; garden not started yet.

Meds: aspirin 81, atorvastatin 40 qhs, lisinopril 20, nifedipine ER 30 (cardiology), mirtazapine 30 qhs, acetaminophen prn. No beta blocker since 4/2024.
Allergy: iodinated contrast, anaphylactoid.

Exam: BP 132/78, other vitals normal. Comfortable. Neck veins flat. Heart regular, no murmur, rub or gallop. Lungs clear, no crackles or wheeze. Abdomen soft, nontender, no hepatosplenomegaly, no ascites, no bruits, normal bowel sounds. Legs: 2+ pitting edema both ankles to mid-shin, symmetric, no redness or warmth, calves soft and non-tender. Reflexes and strength normal.

Data today: ECG normal sinus rhythm. CXR clear, no congestion, heart size normal. Labs drawn: CMP with LFTs, UA.

Assessment: bilateral dependent edema starting weeks after nifedipine, with no sign of heart failure, clot, kidney or liver cause on exam; pending labs, this is calcium channel blocker edema.

Plan:
- Leg elevation in the evening; knee-high compression stockings, prescription given.
- I'd like to talk to his cardiologist before changing the nifedipine, since he is off beta blockers and it seems to be helping his angina. Will call.
- Return precautions: dyspnea, one-sided leg swelling or pain.
- Recheck 3 months.

documents.title: Call with cardiology; patient update
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Spoke with his cardiologist. Agrees with nifedipine edema. With beta blockers off the table after the AV block and his angina better on nifedipine, they prefer to keep it at 30 mg and treat the swelling with stockings and elevation. They will see him in the spring.
Labs from 3/10: creatinine normal, liver tests normal, UA negative.
Called Paul and told him both. He's fine with stockings, his daughter already bought a pair. Keep nifedipine. Follow up in June or sooner if the swelling worsens.

conditions.label: Second degree atrioventricular block, Mobitz type I

medications.drug: 24 HR metoprolol succinate 50 MG Extended Release Oral Tablet
medications.reason: Coronary artery disease after NSTEMI; paced

reports.text: Complete AV dissociation: regular P waves march through without conduction, with a regular junctional escape rhythm at 42. QRS narrow. No acute ST elevation.

Left ventricle normal in size with normal wall thickness. Mild hypokinesis of the inferior wall; remaining segments contract normally. LVEF 50% by biplane method. Right ventricle normal size and function. No significant valvular disease. No pericardial effusion. IVC normal with normal respiratory variation.
reports.conclusion: LVEF 50% with inferior wall hypokinesis. No significant valve disease.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital ED. Faxed 04/03/2025. Date of service 04/01/2025.
CC: collapse.
HPI: 71-year-old man with CAD and prior LAD stent, Mobitz I block a year ago, found on the kitchen floor by himself this morning after going down on the way to the kitchen. Brief loss of consciousness. Tired, no chest pain reported.
Home meds per patient list (copied from prior visit): aspirin, atorvastatin, lisinopril, metoprolol succinate 50 mg, nifedipine ER 30 mg, mirtazapine, acetaminophen prn.
Allergies: iodinated contrast (anaphylactoid).
Exam: pulse 42, BP 88/60, RR 16. Alert, fatigued. Distant heart sounds, otherwise unremarkable heart and lung exam. No trauma.
ECG: complete heart block, junctional escape 42.
ED course: transcutaneous pacing pads with capture, then temporary transvenous pacing wire by cardiology. BP improved with pacing. Initial labs sent.
Disposition: admitted to cardiology CCU.

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Regional hospital, cardiology service. Admitted 04/01/2025, discharged 04/05/2025. Received 05/02/2025 after records request.

Principal diagnosis: third-degree AV block with syncope.
Secondary: non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction; CAD s/p LAD drug-eluting stent 2020; hypertension; hyperlipidemia; iodinated contrast allergy; depression in partial remission.

Hospital course:
1. Complete heart block: presented with syncope, escape rate 42 and hypotension. Paced transcutaneously then by temporary transvenous wire. Block persisted off all AV-nodal agents. Dual-chamber permanent pacemaker implanted 04/03/2025 via left subclavian approach without complication. Device interrogation at discharge normal.
2. NSTEMI: high-sensitivity troponin I peaked at 1,860 ng/L. Coronary angiography 04/02/2025 after premedication with prednisone and diphenhydramine for his prior contrast reaction; no reaction this time. Patent LAD stent. Moderate diffuse disease of the right coronary and circumflex arteries, no lesion suitable for stenting. Medical therapy. Echo: LVEF 50%, inferior hypokinesis, no significant valve disease.
3. Metoprolol: with pacemaker support, metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily restarted for post-MI care.

Discharge medications: aspirin 81 mg daily; atorvastatin 40 mg nightly; metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily (restarted); lisinopril 20 mg daily; nifedipine ER 30 mg daily; mirtazapine 30 mg nightly; acetaminophen 500 mg q6h prn.
Allergies: iodinated contrast media, anaphylactoid; premedicate.
Instructions: no lifting the left arm above shoulder or more than 10 lb for 4 weeks. Wound check in device clinic 7-10 days. Cardiology follow-up 4-6 weeks. PCP within 1 week.

documents.title: Daughter called
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Daughter called to let us know Dad was admitted yesterday after passing out again; heart rate very slow, a temporary pacing wire is in and they are talking about a permanent pacemaker. Also told her he had "a small heart attack." She will update us. Records request sent to the hospital. PCP notified.

documents.title: Post-hospital visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM visit. Daughter with him. Discharge summary not yet received; reviewed the ED fax and his discharge instruction sheet, which he brought.

Per the sheet and the patient: admitted 4/1-4/5 with complete heart block after passing out at home. Temporary wire, then a dual-chamber pacemaker 4/3. Troponin went up and he was told he had a heart attack; the cath (premedicated, no reaction) showed the old stent open and no new stent placed. Metoprolol 50 mg was restarted now that he has a pacemaker.

Since home: no lightheadedness, no chest pain, sore at the device site. Keeping the left arm down. Ankles a little puffy at night, wearing the stockings.

Med reconciliation against the discharge sheet: aspirin 81, atorvastatin 40, metoprolol succinate 50 daily (restarted), lisinopril 20, nifedipine ER 30, mirtazapine 30, acetaminophen prn. He has all of them at home. Contrast allergy confirmed.

Exam: vitals reviewed. Left upper chest incision clean, dry, edges together, small bruise, no swelling. Heart regular (paced). Lungs clear. Trace to 1+ ankle edema, symmetric.

A/P:
1. Complete heart block s/p dual-chamber pacemaker: device clinic wound check scheduled 4/14. Arm precautions.
2. NSTEMI on top of known CAD: continue aspirin, atorvastatin, metoprolol, lisinopril. Cardiology 5/2025.
3. Nifedipine edema: improved with stockings.
4. Mood: says it was scary but he is ok; will screen at next visit.
BMP and CBC today. Discharge summary requested again. RTC 2 months.

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Two and a half months after the pacemaker. Feels good, no fainting, no palpitations. Chest pressure uncommon now, maybe twice since April. Cardiology saw him in May, no changes. Back in the garden, smaller this year. Mood ok, PHQ-9 5, sleeping well.
Discharge summary from April finally arrived 5/2, reviewed.
Exam: vitals reviewed. Pacemaker pocket well healed. Heart regular. Lungs clear. 1+ ankle edema with stockings off; he wears them most days.
A/P: CAD after NSTEMI, angina well controlled on metoprolol plus nifedipine. Pacemaker for complete heart block, device clinic following. HTN controlled. Nifedipine edema stable, continue stockings. MDD partial remission on mirtazapine 30. AWV in September.

documents.title: Pacemaker check
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outside cardiology device clinic. In-office interrogation 07/17/2025, dual-chamber pacemaker implanted 04/03/2025.
Underlying rhythm: sinus with intermittent complete AV block; ventricular pacing a large share of the time.
Lead impedances, sensing and thresholds stable and within normal limits. Battery good. No atrial or ventricular high-rate episodes recorded.
Wound healed.
Impression: normally functioning dual-chamber pacemaker. Remote monitoring enrolled. Next in-office check in 6 months.

documents.body:

HRA: independent in ADLs/IADLs, drives, mows his own lawn, walks the dog twice a day. No falls. Lives alone, daughter nearby. Alcohol 1-2/wk.

Exam: vitals reviewed. Heart regular, paced. Lungs clear. Trace ankle edema. Knees unchanged.
Prevention: LDCT due 11/2025, ordered. Colon UTD to 2028. Flu and COVID next month. Health care proxy on file (daughter).
Labs: CMP, lipids, CBC, A1c.
A/P: chronic problems stable. RTC 4 months.

documents.title: Emergency department physician record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department. Faxed 10/14/2025. Date of service 10/06/2025.

CC: passed out mowing the lawn.
HPI: 72-year-old man with CAD, NSTEMI in April of this year, prior AV block with a dual-chamber pacemaker since April, brought by EMS. A neighbor saw him go down behind the mower; he was out briefly and woke up weak and dizzy. EMS found him hypotensive with a regular pulse of 160.
Meds: aspirin, atorvastatin, metoprolol succinate 50 mg, lisinopril, nifedipine ER, mirtazapine, acetaminophen prn.
Allergies: iodinated contrast media (anaphylactoid).
Exam: confused, slow to answer, BP 74/46 and HR 160 despite IV fluid bolus en route and on arrival.
ECG: wide-complex tachycardia, rate 160.
Course: hemodynamically unstable wide-complex tachycardia, treated as VT. Sedated and given one synchronized shock, converting to sinus rhythm with ventricular pacing. Mental status cleared within minutes; BP 108/66. Potassium, magnesium and troponin normal.
Impression: sustained ventricular tachycardia with syncope and shock, 6 months after MI.
Disposition: admitted to cardiology for electrophysiology evaluation and probable defibrillator upgrade. No driving.

documents.title: Post-hospital visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM. Daughter drove him. ED record received 10/14; no discharge summary yet.

Per ED record and patient: 10/6 passed out mowing, VT at 160 with low pressure, one shock in the ED. Admitted; echo with the same pumping function as April. On 10/9 the pacemaker was swapped for a defibrillator (he calls it "the upgraded box"). Home 10/10. Told no driving for 6 months. Metoprolol same dose.

Now: sore at the device site, otherwise feels normal. No palpitations, no lightheadedness, no shocks. A bit shaken. Sleeping ok. Denies low mood beyond being "rattled"; daughter agrees he's himself.

Meds unchanged from discharge per patient: aspirin 81, atorvastatin 40, metoprolol succinate 50, lisinopril 20, nifedipine ER 30, mirtazapine 30, acetaminophen prn.

Exam: vitals reviewed. Left chest incision clean and closed, mild bruising, no fluctuance. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Trace ankle edema.

A/P:
1. VT s/p ICD upgrade: device clinic follow-up arranged by cardiology. Reviewed what to do if shocked: one shock and feels fine, call cardiology the same day; more than one or feels unwell, 911.
2. No driving for 6 months (until April); daughter and a neighbor are covering rides.
3. CAD post-NSTEMI, HTN: unchanged.
4. Flu shot today. COVID at pharmacy.
Records request for the discharge summary and implant report. RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Defibrillator check
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outside cardiology device clinic. Visit 12/04/2025.
History: dual-chamber pacemaker 04/2025 for complete heart block; sustained ventricular tachycardia with syncope 10/06/2025 requiring cardioversion. On 10/09/2025 the pacemaker generator was replaced with a dual-chamber ICD and a defibrillator lead was added, for secondary prevention. (Implant report on file at the hospital.)
Interrogation: normal device function. Lead parameters stable. Battery good. No treated ventricular arrhythmias, no shocks or ATP since implant. Ventricular pacing frequent, as expected.
Incision well healed.
Plan: remote monitoring every 3 months, in-office check in 6 months. Continue metoprolol. Driving restriction through early April 2026.
